names.note: The name as days.pravoslavie.ru's name page 2184 gives it, «Феодор Иорданский, прп.», with the rank word taken off. Measured with the gate's own fold before it was written: 'иорданскии феодор' has no holder in the corpus. **The day line and the name page call him two different things**: the line «Феодора чудотворца», the wonderworker, and the name page «Феодор Иорданский», of the Jordan. Чудотворец is in BRIEF-RUSSIAN §6's list of rank words and is the `wonderworker` this folder carries in `types`, so the toponymic is what is stored; a bare «Феодор» would meet the hundred-odd Theodore folders this corpus holds.

death.note: The day line closes with the bare century, «(VI)», and `life1239` opens with the same, «жил в VI веке». No year is given anywhere on either page, and no year of birth.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 5 июня ст. ст. — «Прп. Феодора чудотворца (VI).»

attestations.note: The day's fourth entry of twelve, «Прп. Феодора чудотворца (VI).», with `life1239` behind it, a reading of four sentences read whole. `ls -d saints/theodore-the-wonder*` and `saints/theodore-of-jordan*` returned nothing, and the corpus's hundred-odd Theodore folders were measured against the stored form with `fk.mjs` rather than read: 'иорданскии феодор' has no holder. The day page prints eleven hymns, for two Solovki abbots, a bishop of Tyre, a prince of Chernigov, a metropolitan of Kyiv and a prince of Novgorod, and none under his name. His name page lists «День памяти: 5 июня» and nothing else. azbyka.ru was not read.
